what: THE EDGE FROM A CANON ENTITY TO THE ADAPTATION RECORD THAT TOUCHES IT, and from an adaptation to the text it was made from. §VI `relationships/adaptation_mapping/`, which the coverage table records as MISSING because nothing mapped a canon entity to its adaptation.
this_file_does_not_build_the_adaptation_: site/arda_adaptations.json and site/arda_fanon.json hold it -- 76 works, 14 deviations each carrying evidence on both sides, 11 fan claims each with its corpus verdict measured by map/ardatext.py. This file adds EDGES and nothing else, and every edge points at a row those files already hold, by that row's own id.
tier_is_not_an_adaptation_flag: NOTHING HERE IS DERIVED FROM `tier`. t4 means NO INDEPENDENT AUTHORITY -- a wiki, a companion, a guide. It does not mean ADAPTATION and it does not mean FANON, and synthesising a layer out of it would put Robert Foster's Complete Guide in the same bucket as a Peter Jackson film. The layer is a PATH: §IX audits 4 and 5 hunt for adaptation and fanon facts sitting in canonical records, and an audit about a row in the wrong FILE cannot be satisfied by a FLAG on a row still in the wrong file.

the_edge_kinds.deviation names entity: a named divergence whose own prose names a canon entity. The claim is that the DEVIATION RECORD names it -- `matched_in` says which field and `whose_words` says whose wording that field is. The edge does not restate what the deviation says and adds no reading of its own.
the_edge_kinds.work adapted from the text: a work's own `based_on`, resolved to a TIER-1 corpus volume by complete word-prefix -- the route site/arda_place_ids.json already uses and publishes.
the_edge_kinds.work adapted from an adaptation: a `based_on` that names another work in the same file. The Hobbit trilogy and An Unexpected Journey are both films, and an edge from one to Tolkien's text would be false.

why_conf_is_EXT_and_no_row_carries_a_tie: the tiers rank claims about ARDA and an adaptation makes a claim about a FILM. Nothing in this file is evidence about Middle-earth. Both source files declare the same thing in their own words.
not_resolved_is_published_with_its_reaso: `The Two Towers` names no tier-1 volume in this corpus, because the corpus holds The Lord of the Rings as ONE book. That is a fact about the shelf and not a failure, and it is published rather than matched loosely -- a looser match would be this file choosing which book a film adapts.

the_match.vocabulary: map/ardaentity.py, from the collections that DEFINE entity ids.
the_match.comparison: whole words through ardatext.words_of, the archive's ONE matcher.

fields.adaptation_side.shows: what the adaptation shows -- this archive's own summary
fields.adaptation_side.corroboration_anchor: the corroborating source's wording, carried with its hand and licence in arda_adaptations.json
fields.text_side.note: this archive's note on what the text does
fields.text_side.quote_of_the_corpus: Tolkien's own words, verified by map/ardatext.py when arda_adaptations.json was built
fields.claim: the belief, in this archive's own words
fields.ancestry: where the belief is recorded to have come from

the_match.fields_are_named_one_at_a_time: a walk of the record would sweep in source_url, licence_as_stated and capture_sha256, and a name matched inside a URL is not a name.
the_match.containment: where one matched name is inside another, only the longer stands.
the_match.ambiguity: published with every candidate and no winner -- the owner's ruling of 5 August.

mapping_stoplist_why: names that are also ordinary words of film criticism. Measured by running the match with the list empty and reading what it caught.
edges_what: One row per edge. `entity` resolves in the collection named beside it; `adaptation_record` names the dataset, the collection and the row id it points at, in a field called `record_id` and NEVER `id`: map/xref_census.py calls a record `anything carrying id or key`, so a reference written as `id` would read as this file DEFINING the deviation it points at -- a reference wearing a definition's clothes, in a census whose whole subject is telling those apart. A work-to-source edge carries no entity and says so with a null.
